title:
The Supreme Court Rebuffs Trump on Research Grants.
Trump Meets Quad Allies in Manila.
A Crimean Bridge Span Falls After a Ukraine Strike.
subject: Supreme Court Rebuffs Trump on Research Grant Cuts
preview_text: Trump meets Quad allies in Manila, bank apps stall and Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge.
description: Two Supreme Court orders, Trump's Quad meeting in Manila, a bank outage and a European deportation plan for Rwanda.
contents_extra: Why the Crimean Bridge collapse matters, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Supreme Court Turns Away a Trump Grant Appeal and a Gun Challenge

photo.alt: The US Supreme Court building in Washington; file photo.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a Trump administration appeal over canceled research grants. NBC News reports the move leaves in place rulings that the cuts violated free speech rights. The grants went to University of California researchers.

The administration had deemed the projects inconsistent with its policies, including its opposition to DEI. The government tried to end $324 million in funding to University of California institutions. Some of that funding has since resumed.

The justices also declined to hear a broad challenge to Maryland's gun limits. The restrictions cover state parks, public transport, schools, healthcare facilities and places that sell alcohol. Those rules now remain in place.

Why it matters. The orders leave lower court rulings intact on two hot-button issues. Justice Clarence Thomas signaled interest in a more narrowly focused gun case. He said he is skeptical the Maryland provisions are lawful.

stories.title: Trump Lands in Manila for His First Quad Meeting of the Second Term

photo.alt: A city skyline across the water at sunset; illustrative file photo, not Manila.

paragraphs: President Donald Trump landed in Manila on Tuesday for the ASEAN summit. ABC News reports he touched down at 5:33 p.m. local time after over 18 hours of travel. About 300 performers greeted him on the tarmac.

Trump then flew by helicopter to meet leaders of Australia, India and Japan. NBC News reports it is his first Quad leaders' meeting since returning to office. The talks, the group's first summit in two years, were under way as of 6:10 a.m. ET.

Trump told reporters the four countries have a great relationship. BBC News reports a separate meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi looks unlikely. The two countries are still negotiating a trade deal.

Why it matters. The Quad is a security grouping of key US partners in the Indo-Pacific. Trump is due to fly to Shenzhen on Wednesday for an Asia-Pacific summit. He is set to hold a three-way meeting there with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: A Chase Software Bug Slows Banking for Customers Across the Country

photo.alt: A standalone ATM machine indoors; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: Customers at several major US banks reported trouble reaching their accounts on Monday. CBS News reports nearly 4,800 users had reported problems with Chase by 2 p.m. ET. Complaints also rose at Bank of America, Wells Fargo and others.

Chase blamed a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware systems. A JPMorgan spokesperson told CNBC there is no evidence it is cyber-related. The bank said customers could still access their accounts and funds.

Chase said other banks may have slowed only when they were party to a transaction with it. Users also reported problems with the payments app Zelle. Downdetector showed service back to normal early Tuesday.

Why it matters. Chase is the largest bank in the country. BBC News reports it serves more than 86 million customers at 5,000 branches. The glitch follows recent outages at Microsoft and in air traffic systems.

stories.title: Five European Countries Plan a Deportation Center in Rwanda

photo.alt: Hillside homes in Kigali, Rwanda; file photo.

paragraphs: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands announced a plan on Monday to open a return hub in Rwanda. BBC News reports it is expected to accept transfers in 2027.

The scheme would cover migrants with enforceable removal orders, including rejected asylum seekers. Al Jazeera reports the five governments would cover the costs, including temporary accommodation. A formal agreement has yet to be signed.

Deportees could settle in Rwanda or return to their home countries. Unlike a scrapped British deal, it applies only to people who have exhausted legal avenues to stay. Spain's Pedro Sanchez said the plan had no future or humanity.

Why it matters. European governments are under pressure to speed up removals. Officials said last year about 90 percent of rejected applicants remain in the bloc. Rights groups warn the plan could expose vulnerable people to abuse.

deep_dive.title: What the Crimean Bridge Collapse Means for Russia's War Effort

photo.alt: An arch bridge over a river in Croatia; illustrative file photo, not Crimea.

paragraphs: Ukraine severely damaged the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea overnight. BBC News reports a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water. The Guardian reports a 227-meter road arch span appears to have fallen into the Kerch Strait. The adjacent railway arch was also damaged.

Russia built the bridge after it annexed Crimea in 2014, and Putin personally opened it in 2018. BBC News says the risk of a serious logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased. Traffic out of Crimea now relies on a land corridor exposed to Ukrainian drones. Debris appears to block the main shipping channel beneath it.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the strike capped a seven-stage operation weeks in the making. Crimea's Kremlin-appointed governor said traffic on the bridge had been suspended. He asked residents to avoid traveling toward it. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be restored and would be even better than before.

Ukraine hit the bridge with a truck bomb in 2022 and a sea drone the following year. Pro-war Russian commentators warned that repairs would be very difficult this time, because Ukraine can now strike floating cranes and repair crews. Al Jazeera reports Ukraine held new peace talks with US and European officials on Monday. The strike comes as Putin prepares to meet the US and Chinese leaders.

trivia.question: In what year was the Crimean Bridge opened?
trivia.explanation: C. 2018. BBC News reports Vladimir Putin personally opened the bridge in 2018.

poll.question: Should the US deepen security ties with its Quad partners in Asia?

World view: More tankers hit near Hormuz. Iran's navy said tankers struck mines, while a UK agency reported two attacks on Monday; Al Jazeera reports.
Peace talks head to Berlin. Zelensky said talks with US envoys and Europe were not easy, but participants agreed to meet in Berlin; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: ICE arrest video draws scrutiny. A lawyer says agents pepper-sprayed a pregnant US citizen and threw her to the ground in Modesto, California; ABC News reports.
Trump flew the Qatari jet to Asia. Questions linger about security upgrades to the plane, two US officials said; NBC News reports.
Money & markets: Futures slip before Nvidia results. S&P 500 futures were 0.29% lower around 6 a.m. ET Tuesday after the Dow slid more than 700 points Monday; CNBC reports.
The dollar hits a 19-month high. It rose to its highest since April 2025 on bets for tighter Fed policy; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Commerce closes a chip loophole. A new rule targets Chinese firms leasing Nvidia computing power from data centers abroad; CNBC reports.
Nvidia adds a security committee. The new committee will oversee national security and export control compliance; NBC News reports.
The score: Lukaku retires from Belgium duty. The record scorer ends 16 years with 94 goals in 135 games; Al Jazeera reports.
Alonso returns to the Dakar. The two-time F1 champion, 45, will race the January rally in an Aston Martin entry; Al Jazeera reports.
Life & culture: Robert Pattinson is the new Bond. Denis Villeneuve will direct the next 007 film, with no title or date yet; BBC News reports.
Pope Leo ends a 12-day tour. Millions turned out in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru weeks after his lung cancer surgery; NBC News reports.
